coverage_notes: All 41 listed files were read completely. 499890.txt appears twice in the list (care-decisions and financial-planning folders) with identical text; both are listed as sources and quotes use the basename 499890.txt. Several saved threads are partial because the page showed more replies than the script captured (498174: 37 shown, 10 captured; 499659: 43 vs 10; 499771: 18 vs 10; 499699: 27 vs 10; 498744: 18 vs 10). Six files have an empty POST body (499331, 499812, 499827, 499766, 499873, 499899), so only comments exist. gap_evidence lists: paying_for_tools has very little (no one mentions paying for a coordination app); the few entries are about unrelated products (a catheter system, a daily money manager, a phone plan). No forum poster described a shared app used among siblings; the only app named was a free care-notes app used with paid aides.

caveats: AgingCare is a support forum, so posts skew toward distress and people who already use online tools; replies collapsed behind See all were not captured, and several long threads are partial (498174, 499659, 499771, 499699, 498744). Many replies are advice from other members, not the original poster's own experience, and some replies quote AI chatbot output or generic web text (498960, 499766). Four threads (499331, 499812, 499827, 499766, 499873, 499899) have no post body, so the poster's own situation is unknown. Theme assignments and family_dynamic labels are my judgment from the text and several are marked unclear. Handles such as names in replies were not quoted. Quotes were copied from the saved files but not re-verified by script.
